title: CEOと工作員の関係 NVIDIA調査
body: アメリカの半導体大手エヌビディアのトップが中国の女性工作員と親密な関係にあったと報じられた問題で、エヌビディアは社内調査を始めると発表しました。【写真で見る】エヌビディア・フアンCEO　今年7月には来日エヌビディアは8日、ジェンスン・フアンCEOが中国のスパイ活動の標的になったとの報道を受け、社内調査を始めると発表しました。アメリカメディアは先月、フアンCEOが中国の女性工作員と親密な関係となり、製品の情報が中国側に伝えられた疑いがあると報じていました。フアン氏は従業員向けのメッセージで「妻を裏切った。弁解の余地はない」と不倫を認めて謝罪し、社内調査に全面的に協力する意向を示しました。エヌビディアは「国家安全保障やエヌビディアの機密情報が侵害されたと考える理由はないが、あらゆる情報を精査する」としています。

title: パラグライダー落下か 72歳死亡
body:
８日午後３時２０分頃、高知県土佐市高岡町の山中で、「パラグライダーが落下した」と１１９番があった。現場には、パラグライダーが木に引っかかった状態で見つかったほか、操縦していた同市の男性会社員（７２）が倒れていた。男性は近くの病院に運ばれたが、死亡が確認された。
県警土佐署によると、男性はパラグライダーの仲間と一緒に同市内のパラグライダー基地から飛び立った。男性が着陸を予定していた場所に姿を見せなかったため、仲間が周辺を捜していたという。同署は男性が落下したとみて調べている。

title: 舎人ライナー 資金不足陥る可能性
body: 朝の混雑率が全国1位の「日暮里・舎人ライナー」について、2033年度にも資金不足に陥る可能性があることが、運行する東京都への取材でわかった。混雑緩和へ様々な対策を迫られている一方、通勤通学時間帯以外の乗客数が伸び悩んでいるためだ。都は運賃の改定も視野に入れている。【さらに詳しく】日暮里・舎人ライナーの「想定外」とは日暮里・舎人ライナーは23区北東部の鉄道空白地域を解消する新交通システムとして、08年に開業したが、経常赤字が長年続いた。建設費の支払いに加え、混雑対策が重荷となったためだ。沿線の宅地開発で人口が想定以上に増えた結果、開業当初から混雑対策が課題となった。都は定員を増やした車両への更新や増発などの手を打ってきたが、こうした支出が大きな負担としてのしかかる。さらに、収益を大きく伸ばしにくい経営環境が足かせになっている。利用客は朝ラッシュ時の日暮里方面に集中しており、反対方向や日中は少ない。住宅地を走り、通勤通学で使う住民が多いため、比較的割安な定期券の利用率が1年あたり約65%と高い。24年度に開業以来初めて経常黒字化を達成したが、都の担当者は「楽観はできない」と話す。今後はさらなる車両更新などで経常赤字に陥り、赤字幅も拡大する見通しで、33年度には資金不足に陥ると見込まれるという。都は収益改善策として、運賃改定についての検討を進める方針だ。（松尾葉奈）

title: 北朝鮮ハッカーのチャットか 入手
body:
ハングルでやりとりされているチャット画面を「バンキシャ！」では入手しました。「北朝鮮のハッカー」が仲間とやりとりしたものとみられるもので、中には、「優先地域はアメリカ・日本」という言葉もみられました。日本で相次ぐサイバー攻撃。果たして、北朝鮮のハッカー集団は関与しているのか。取材で明らかになったのは――。【真相報道バンキシャ！】【動画で見る】“日本も標的”北朝鮮ハッカー集団か“会話”入手　サイバー攻撃の裏側、身近に広がるリスク【バンキシャ！】
8日、都内で開催されていたのは、ジンギスカンなど羊の肉の料理を味わえるイベント。北海道から来たという店主が気にしていたのは……。店主／北海道から出店「ポイントカードとかやってるんですけど、ネット環境に登録したくないという人は増えてきているかな。お店としても勧めてはいけない時期なのかなと考えています」5日、NTTドコモは最大およそ30万件の顧客情報が流出したと発表。一部顧客については、口座番号なども含まれるという。また「良品計画」は、現在も有効なクレジットカード番号およそ34万5000件が流出した可能性があると発表した。海外でも深刻な被害が出ている。暗号資産大手・バイナンスでは、およそ1兆円の暗号資産が被害にあった。この事件について、FBIは、北朝鮮のハッカー集団が関与したと断定。北朝鮮側はこれを否定している。いま、日本で相次ぐサイバー攻撃。そこに北朝鮮は関与しているのか。
7日、バンキシャ！は韓国へ飛んだ。北朝鮮のサイバー攻撃を研究するキムさんは、韓国国防省が管轄する研究所で40年以上分析を続けている。キム･ヨルス氏／韓国軍事問題研究院「北朝鮮にはトレイダートレイターという組織やラザルス、APT38などといった名前のハッカー集団が存在します。海外で活動しているハッカーは3000人以上と言われています」4年前に北朝鮮の国営テレビで放送された映像には、パソコンに向かう学生とみられる姿が映っていた。キムさんに見せると──。キム･ヨルス氏／韓国軍事問題研究院「金策工業総合大学。（北朝鮮では）小学生の段階で数学やコンピューターに優れた児童を選抜します。そして基礎を固めてから、大学でサイバー専門教育を受けさせます。一部は軍に送られ、一部は海外へ出て、暗号資産や情報を盗むようになるんです」キムさんによると、軍の傘下などで活動するハッカーは、北朝鮮内での地位も高いという。キム･ヨルス氏／韓国軍事問題研究院「（ハッカーになると）高い給料をもらえます。（ハッキングで）盗んだお金の5～10％が自分のものになります」

title: 欧州右派政党 トランプ氏離れ鮮明
body:
米中間選挙でトランプ大統領率いる与党・共和党が大敗したことを受け、これまでトランプ氏に共鳴してきた欧州各国の右派政党が距離を置く姿勢を鮮明にしている。物価高に対応できなかったトランプ氏と関連づけられることを嫌っているとみられ、その引き金となったイラン攻撃に対しても批判を強めている。【写真】トランプ氏の不倫相手とされる元ポルノ女優
「驚くべき結果だ」。トランプ氏を称賛し、共和党との連携を深めてきたドイツの強硬右派政党「ドイツのための選択肢（ＡｆＤ）」のアリス・ワイデル共同党首は４日、独ＤＰＡ通信などの取材に衝撃を隠さなかった。
ワイデル氏は、トランプ氏が「米国第一」を掲げて介入主義的な外交政策は行わないと有権者に約束したものの、「その公約を破ったことが裏目に出た」と指摘。共和党の敗北について、「イラン戦争の壊滅的な影響が主な原因だ」と突き放した。
ＡｆＤは、トランプ氏の「米国を再び偉大に（ＭＡＧＡ）」運動を手本とし、「ドイツを再び偉大に」といったスローガンを掲げて支持を広げてきた。それでも、イラン攻撃に関しては独経済への打撃も大きく、ワイデル氏としても無視できなかった模様だ。
これまでトランプ氏とのパイプを誇示してきた英国の右派ポピュリスト政党「改革党」のナイジェル・ファラージ党首も５日、記者団に「イラン攻撃が誤りだったのは明白だ。トランプ氏は『戦争はしない』とする有権者との約束を破った」と述べ、トランプ氏の判断に疑問を呈した。
極右の流れをくむフランスの右派政党「国民連合」のジョルダン・バルデラ党首は４日、地元ラジオで「私は米国の有権者ではない。他国で起きたことは関係ない」と強調した。
同党の実質的指導者であるマリーヌ・ルペン氏は、過去の米大統領選でトランプ氏支持を表明したこともあるが、今回の中間選挙を巡っては表立ったコメントを控えている。来春の仏大統領選の最有力候補と目される中、沈黙を守るのが得策との判断とみられる。

title: 米大統領 戦闘再開「可能性低い」
body:
（CNN）　トランプ米大統領は8日、米国によるイランとの戦闘再開について、イランの核開発計画とホルムズ海峡再開を巡る交渉に進展がある限り、自身がそれを命じることになる可能性は「極めて低い」と述べた。CNNのインタビューの中で、この主張を5回繰り返した。「非常に強力な合意に署名するかどうかにかかっている」。CNNとの20分間の電話インタビューで,トランプ氏はイランについてそう語った。「答えは、（攻撃再開が）必要になる可能性は極めて低いということだ。イランは破綻（はたん）国家だ。今年発表されたばかりだが、インフレ率は301%だ。必要になる可能性は極めて低い。必要であればそうするだろうが、我々はイランに非常に厳しい打撃を与えた。それがどれほど厳しいものだったか、あなた方は知らないだろう」「だから、そうする必要が生じる可能性は極めて低い」とトランプ大統領は続けた。「イランは財政的に衰退している。我々は軍事的に打撃を与えた。イランを完全に打ち負かすこともできた」
戦闘の開始から8カ月、これまで終結への意欲について矛盾した発言もしてきたトランプ氏は、インタビューの中で、攻撃命令が出れば米軍は地域に展開できる態勢にあると明言。「準備はできている。空母が3隻ある。もう1隻も到着したばかりだ」とし、すでに配備している3隻は「準備万端だ」と述べた。トランプ氏はまた、軍事行動が再開された場合に備え、イラン国内の発電所や橋などのインフラ施設を標的として特定していると明らかにした。38の橋に対して、「文字通り1時間で破壊できる」状況にあるという。一方で、イランのインフラ施設を破壊することは望まないとも述べ、「橋の再建には10年かかるので、破壊したくはない」と言い添えた。
米軍の攻撃再開に対するイランの防衛能力について、トランプ氏は「イランの防空システムは破壊された」と主張。「対空兵器が全くないので、攻撃は止められない。対空兵器は全て失われた」との見解を示した。その上で、イランのミサイルとドローン（無人機）の備蓄状況についても新たな詳細を明らかにした。それによるとイラン側が維持しているミサイルとドローンの生産能力は、それぞれ戦闘開始前の10％、15％の水準に落ち込んでいるという。「新たな軍事行動が必要になる公算は極めて小さい」「彼らはどうしても合意を成立させたいと考えている」。トランプ氏は改めてそう付け加えた。

title: トランプ氏 UFC代表に報道官打診
body:
【ワシントン共同】トランプ米大統領は7日、総合格闘技団体UFCのダナ・ホワイト最高経営責任者（CEO）に、大統領報道官への就任を打診したと交流サイト（SNS）で明らかにした。ホワイト氏を「凶暴なファイターで戦士だ」と持ち上げ「どうかこの仕事を引き受けて」と書き込んだ。【写真】ビル・ゲイツ氏が暴露したトランプ氏の「無知さ」　18年
ホワイト氏はトランプ氏と親交が深く、有力な支持者として知られる。今年6月にはトランプ氏の誕生日に合わせて、ホワイトハウス南庭でUFCの試合を開催した。トランプ氏は投稿で、複数の格闘家を「アシスタント」として連れてくるよう要請したと表明。「狂った左翼からわれわれを守るために、こうした人材が必要だ」と主張した。大統領報道官は、第2次トランプ政権発足時から務めたレビット氏が今年8月に退任。今年10月に後任に就いた保守系コメンテーター、ザカリア氏は経歴詐称疑惑が報じられてわずか5日で去り、空席となっている。

title: 露衛星の軍事利用開始か ウ警戒
body:
【キーウ共同】ウクライナ国防省情報総局の関係者は7日、ロシアが構築を進める衛星通信サービス「ラススベト（夜明け）」の軍事利用をウクライナ領内で開始したと共同通信に明らかにした。運用している小型衛星の数が少ないため利用できる時間は限られているが、ロシア軍の無人機攻撃の精度向上などにつながるとみてウクライナは警戒を強めている。【写真】「ロシア兵器9割に日本部品」　ミサイルや無人機に転用　名指しされた日本企業13社
ラススベトは、米宇宙開発企業スペースXの「スターリンク」への対抗が目的だとされる。スターリンクは低軌道上に1万機を超える小型衛星を展開させ、ブロードバンドインターネットを提供している。情報総局の関係者はロシア軍がいつどこでラススベトを軍事利用したのかについては明らかにしなかった。ウクライナ軍関係者によると、ロシアは今年3月と7月に北西部のプレセツク宇宙基地から衛星16機ずつ計32機を打ち上げた。衛星の数がまだ少ないため、ウクライナ領内で使用する場合、1日当たり2～4時間半に限られるとみられる。専門家は本格稼働させるには計250機程度が必要だとしている。

title: イスラエル 野党党首に組閣指示
body:
【エルサレム共同】イスラエルのヘルツォグ大統領は8日、10月27日に実施された国会（定数120）総選挙の結果を受け、反ネタニヤフ首相陣営を率いる中道ヤシャルの党首、アイゼンコット元軍参謀総長に組閣を指示した。連立交渉が一段と加速する。退陣の可能性が出ているネタニヤフ氏は「挙国一致内閣」の樹立を呼びかけ、反首相陣営による政権樹立の阻止を試みている。【写真】歴史が生んだ「世紀の難問」…イスラエル、パレスチナの争いはなぜ始まった
連立交渉は立場の異なる政党との連携が必要となることから難航は必至で、予断を許さない。総選挙では、首相在任が通算19年を超えてイスラエル史上最長のネタニヤフ氏による続投の是非が焦点となり、首相陣営と反首相陣営はいずれも過半数には届かなかった。アイゼンコット氏は2023年に始まったパレスチナ自治区ガザでの戦闘で従軍中の息子が死亡し、ネタニヤフ氏への批判を強めた。軍時代には圧倒的な軍事力で敵対勢力を抑えようとした。アイゼンコット氏が新政権を発足させたとしても、イスラエルの安全保障政策が大きく転換するとの見方は少ない。

body: アメリカの半導体大手エヌビディアのトップが中国の女性工作員と親密な関係にあったと報じられた問題で、エヌビディアは社内調査を始めると発表しました。【写真で見る】エヌビディア・フアンCEO　今年7月には来日エヌビディアは8日、ジェンスン・フアンCEOが中国のスパイ活動の標的になったとの報道を受け、社内調査を始めると発表しました。アメリカメディアは先月、フアンCEOが中国の女性工作員と親密な関係となり、製品の情報が中国側に伝えられた疑いがあると報じていました。フアン氏は従業員向けのメッセージで「妻を裏切った。弁解の余地はない」と不倫を認めて謝罪し、社内調査に全面的に協力する意向を示しました。エヌビディアは「国家安全保障やエヌビディアの機密情報が侵害されたと考える理由はないが、あらゆる情報を精査する」としています。

title: MAZDA3セダン 北米で売れる理由
body:
マツダの北米事業を統括する「マツダノースアメリカンオペレーションズ（MNAO）」は3日、10月の北米の販売台数を発表しました。【画像を見る】北米で販売台数を大幅に増やしているMAZDA3MNAOによりますと、10月の総販売台数は3万1446台で、前年同月比で25％増加しました。なかでもMAZDA3は3534台と、前年同月1440台から大幅に増加しています。北米でのMAZDA3の販売は、今年5月以降好調を維持していて、5月は4121台（1668台増）、6月は3787台（1881台増）、7月は3903台（1821台増）8月は4427台（2118台増）、9月は3704台（2204台増）と、前年同月を大きく上回る販売が続いています。■MAZDA3はアメリカでなぜ売れている?　マツダが挙げる“3”つの理由特にMAZDA3の「セダン」は、10月の販売台数が2606台と、前年同月の920台を大きく上回っています。なぜ、今北米でMAZDA3が売れているのでしょうか。マツダは3つの理由をあげています。（1）市場環境とのマッチ理由の第1は「市場環境とのマッチ」です。マツダは「物価・金利高、ガソリン価格高止まりの中で、『購入しやすい価格帯の小型車』、『燃料コストを抑えやすいコンパクトカー』への需要が拡大していて、そのニーズにMAZDA3がフィットしている」としています。■第2の理由は、まさに「マツダらしい」もの次にマツダが挙げるのは、まさに「マツダらしい」とも言える「商品力の高さ」です。（2）商品力の高さ「デザイン、上質な室内空間、安全性能、人馬一体の走りといったコンパクトカーでも妥協したくない価値をバランス良く備えており、米国でも『安全なブランド』としての評価（※IIHS:日本のJNCAPのような外部評価）で、高評価を獲得したことも追い風になっています」■最後にあげられたのは、組織として強さなぜMAZDA3が北米で売れているのか。マツダが3つめに挙げたのは、販売・供給戦略です。
（3）戦略的な販売・供給の取り組み「需要の高いマーケットに販売・マーケティング施策を集中し、継続的に強化しています。MAZDA3を『購入しやすい価格帯の成長軸』と位置づけた中期的戦略のもと、販促やインセンティブを運用。関税環境を踏まえた生産地切替などにより、競争力と供給安定性を確保しています」「市場環境」「商品力」「マーケティング施策」。マツダは、これら3つが組み合わさることで、MAZDA3の北米での販売が堅調に推移しているとしています。

title: 倉庫には古米の山 赤字覚悟で販売
body: ■倉庫には“古米の山” 販売店「かつてない量」今も価格が下がり続けているコメ。一時の高騰は収まりましたが、実は在庫が大変なことになっているようです。そして、日本のコメを支える中山間地域の農家の今を取材しました。【写真を見る】倉庫には“古米の山” 販売店「かつてない量」 新米より古米が高い逆転現象… 赤字覚悟で販売愛知県岡崎市にある「渡辺米穀店」。店頭には、新米と去年とれた古米の両方が並んでいます。（渡辺米穀店 渡邊正明店主）Q.青森県産「あさゆき」（玄米1キロ840円）の古米は去年いくらだった?「900円くらい」Q.840円くらいまでしか下げられない理由は?「仕入れ値が高かった」去年までのコメ不足による価格の高止まりから一転、コメ余りで新米が古米よりも安い「価格の逆転現象」が起きています。（渡辺米穀店 渡邊正明店主）「ここまで（古米が）余っていることはない。価格差がこれだけあることは今までなかった」■「持っていても…」赤字覚悟で古米を安売りスーパーでの販売価格は、ことし始めに最高値の5キロ4400円台になったものの、そこから下落。9月以降は2000円台になり、最新の価格は2821円（10月12日〜18日）です。（渡辺米穀店 渡邊正明店主）「古米を持っていても…処分価格になっている」在庫の古米は、赤字覚悟で売るしかありません。（渡辺米穀店 渡邊正明店主）Q.例年、去年のコメがこの時期にたくさんある?「ないです。あったとしても2列くらい、多くても3列くらいまで。こんなにあることは、いまだかつてない」去年多めに買い入れたため、例年だとほとんどなくなっているはずの古米の膨大な在庫が。（渡辺米穀店 渡邊正明店主）「値段差が大きく変わることや、コメがないとかあんまり経験がないので、この先どのように立ち回っていくのか契約部分も含めて難しくなってきた」■ITや大型機械の利用困難 中山間地域のコメ農家価格の変動が激しく、「業」としては不安定と言えるコメ作り。今どのような状況にあるのか。大規模化やIT導入の恩恵を受けづらい、中山間地域のコメ農家を訪ねました。（KINOファーム 木下貴晴代表）Q.コメ価格が下がり、やっていけないという農家はいる?「この状態では続けられない農家が増えると思う」豊田市下山地区のKINOファーム。代表の木下さんは、8年前に脱サラをして専業農家になりました。

title: 舎人ライナー 資金不足陥る可能性
body: 朝の混雑率が全国1位の「日暮里・舎人ライナー」について、2033年度にも資金不足に陥る可能性があることが、運行する東京都への取材でわかった。混雑緩和へ様々な対策を迫られている一方、通勤通学時間帯以外の乗客数が伸び悩んでいるためだ。都は運賃の改定も視野に入れている。【さらに詳しく】日暮里・舎人ライナーの「想定外」とは日暮里・舎人ライナーは23区北東部の鉄道空白地域を解消する新交通システムとして、08年に開業したが、経常赤字が長年続いた。建設費の支払いに加え、混雑対策が重荷となったためだ。沿線の宅地開発で人口が想定以上に増えた結果、開業当初から混雑対策が課題となった。都は定員を増やした車両への更新や増発などの手を打ってきたが、こうした支出が大きな負担としてのしかかる。さらに、収益を大きく伸ばしにくい経営環境が足かせになっている。利用客は朝ラッシュ時の日暮里方面に集中しており、反対方向や日中は少ない。住宅地を走り、通勤通学で使う住民が多いため、比較的割安な定期券の利用率が1年あたり約65%と高い。24年度に開業以来初めて経常黒字化を達成したが、都の担当者は「楽観はできない」と話す。今後はさらなる車両更新などで経常赤字に陥り、赤字幅も拡大する見通しで、33年度には資金不足に陥ると見込まれるという。都は収益改善策として、運賃改定についての検討を進める方針だ。（松尾葉奈）

title: Surgeon having lunch near Krakow shooting undoubtedly saved officer's life, colleague says
summary: Further details have emerged about two police officers hailed for preventing a Polish gunman from killing more.
body:
Watch: Doctor who treated victims of Krakow shooting speaks to the BBC
One of two surgeons who treated victims on the streets in the aftermath of a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland said his colleague "undoubtedly" saved the life of a gravely injured police officer.
The pair were eating near the city's Main Market Square on Saturday when a gunman began firing at random, killing six people and injuring 15.
The doctors raced to treat both the attacker and two officers shot while subduing the perpetrator.
On Sunday, the officers - both hailed as "true heroes" by the prime minister for preventing further deaths - emerged from comas.
Prosecutors launched a terror investigation after ministers previously said the 24-year-old Polish attacker - who remains in a critical condition - was apparently inspired by "far-right ideologies".
A British national and Austrian woman were among those killed alongside four Poles.
Professor Michal Pędziwiatr was having lunch with a colleague, named by local media as Dr Mateusz Wierdak, and their families in central Krakow when they heard gunshots.
Pędziwiatr told the BBC: "We saw the shooting attack. And what a surgeon can do in a situation like this?... We decided to help the victims as soon as possible.
"We rushed into the area where the shooting was and started our rescue, because there were no ambulances available, there were no professionals around."
What we know about the deadly Krakow shooting
He said his colleague used his hand to stem the bleeding from the most injured policeman, allowing them to wait for an ambulance which transferred the officer to hospital.
Pędziwiatr said they came to learn that one of those they treated was the apparent attacker.
"As a doctor... it doesn't matter to me if it's a victim or a suspect," he said.
"It's not our task to decide what to do with this guy... for us, it was another heavily injured victim, that's all."
According to local media, Wierdak is a renowned surgeon in Krakow. The University Hospital in Krakow states Pędziwiatr is head of General, Oncological, Metabolic and Emergency Surgery.
The police officers have been identified as senior constables Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański.
The attacker has not yet been named by authorities.
When his house was searched after the attack in central Krakow, the bodies of his parents and sister were found.
The National Public Prosecutor's Office in Poland launched an investigation into the attack with a unit specialising in "terrorist offences" taking the lead.
Separately, reports emerged that six Dublin Civil Defence volunteers also assisted in the aftermath of the shooting.
Investigations continued in central Krakow on Sunday before Main Market Square reopened
James McConnell, an officer, told RTE News the group were on a city break andwere close to the main square,externalwhen the shooting happened.
The volunteers who are trained to provide medical care immediately sought to help injured people, providing "CPR and haemorrhage control".
Witnesses who were close to the attack described panic and confusion around the square as it unfolded.
Ruby Catherine Warren, from London, heard gunfire and "yelled at my friends to run and we all sprinted for our lives".
Not knowing where the gunman was - or if there was more than one - they "just kept sprinting", eventually finding a hotel to hide inside.
How the deadly shooting in Krakow unfolded
Tom Brook, from West Yorkshire, was inside a McDonald's near the square when he heard "multiple gunshots and saw people running for cover".
"I then walked into the square and saw paramedics working on someone outside [a shop] and there was a dead body covered in foil blankets 20 meters away," he said.
The suspect wore full military tactical gear during the attack and was described as having a military-grade weapon - but the government said he was not a member of the Polish armed forces.
Poland's Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said "everything suggests" the suspect was "fascinated by far-right ideologies" and held ultra-nationalist views.
The rampage began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) on Saturday in the historic centre of Krakow.
Footage showed the attacker's vehicle speeding through the centre of the city, and people fleeing as the sound of gunfire rang out.
The glass fronts of shops were shattered by bullets and a tram was shot at during the attack, which police say lasted for around three minutes.
The mayor of Krakow said he had submitted an urgent request for the two officers injured while stopping the attacker to be awarded titles of honorary citizens of the city.
Main Market Square reopened on Sunday evening after a security cordon was lifted.

title: Seven dead and more than 100 injured after trains collide in Egypt
summary: Several carriages derailed after two trains travelling in the same direction crashed outside the city of Giza.
body:
Footage shows derailed train carriages near Giza in Egypt
At least seven people have died in a train crash near the Egyptian city of Giza, with more than 100 injured.
The country's railway authority said two trains travelling south from Giza and Cairo collided, causing several carriages to derail and fall down an embankment.
Images from the scene showed people looking inside overturned carriages for injured passengers as a massive emergency response was launched.
Egyptian President Abdul Fattah al-Sisi said he had ordered state authorities to "investigate the circumstances of the accident, and hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent".
The public prosecutor's office warned the death toll could rise.
Uninjured passengers and bystanders searched derailed carriages for injured people
The government said hospitals in the area had been put "on heightened alert" as they dealt with a massive influx of patients.
Egypt's health minister Dr Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said people were being treated for broken bones and head injuries.
The Egyptian Red Crescent said it was providing aid and psychological support to victims and their families at the scene.
The driver of one of the trains was among those who died in the crash, the ministry confirmed.
The first train involved in the crash was travelling from Giza to Fayoum, south of Cairo, when it crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to Aswan, which was stationary on the tracks.
Images from the scene showed some carriages had overturned, with the body of at least one appearing to have split in two.
Trains between Giza and the Upper Egypt region were suspended as cranes were dispatched to remove the wrecked trains. The railway authority has not said how long it expects this to take.
The collision occurred in the area between Kafr Ammar and Al-Raqqa stations in Al-Ayyat, close to where Egypt's deadliest train tragedy occurred in February 2002, when a fire engulfed a passenger train travelling from Cairo to Luxor.
In that incident, more than 370 people were officially reported killed, although some estimates put the toll considerably higher.
Two further crashes in the area in 2009 killed dozens more.
There were calls in Egypt on Sunday for the transport minister to resign over the latest deadly rail disaster.
Foreign leaders and dignitaries have shared condolences and support for the victims.
Saudi Arabia's ministry of foreign affairs expressed "solidarity" with Egypt and wished those hurt a speedy recovery.
Turkey's ambassador to Egypt wrote on X that he extended "heartfelt condolences and sincere sympathy" to the victims, their families, and the Egyptian people.

title: Homes and temples glow across India to mark Diwali
summary: Millions of Indians are marking the festival of lights with glowing lamps, fireworks and traditional sweets.
body:
Traditional Diwali oil lamps or diyas
Millions across India are celebratingDiwali, the Hindu festival of lights, illuminating homes, temples, offices and streets with oil lamps and colourful lights to symbolise the triumph of light over darkness.
The festival falls on the darkest night of the Hindu lunar month of Kartik, when the moon is not visible in the sky.
Although Diwali traditions vary across India's regions and communities, the festival is widely marked by prayers, family gatherings, the exchange of sweets and the lighting of firecrackers.
But the celebrations come amid growingconcerns over air pollution, particularly in northern India.
Seasonal weather conditions and the burning of crop residue contribute to deteriorating air quality, while firecrackers set off during Diwali can make the situation worse.
Air pollution in the Indian capital Delhi has reached such hazardous levels that it is the most polluted Diwali festival in a decade. New measures to improve air quality do not seem to have been successful.
India's financial capital, Mumbai, has also experienced high pollution levels in recent weeks.
In an effort to limit pollution, India's Supreme Court on Monday permitted the manufacture, sale and use of certified "green" firecrackers in Delhi and surrounding areas for a limited period.
These firecrackers are designed to produce 20-30% fewer emissions than conventional fireworks. But critics have questioned how effective they are at reducing pollution and raised concerns that conventional firecrackers could still make their way into the capital from neighbouring states.
Repeated violations of firecracker restrictions leave cities grappling with worsening post-Diwali smog
Despite the debate over fireworks, Diwali is about much more than firecrackers.
The festival celebrates the return of Lord Ram to Ayodhya after his victory over Ravan, the main antagonist in the Hindu epic Ramayana, and symbolises the triumph of good over evil, light over darkness, and knowledge over ignorance.
In the days leading up to the festival, families clean and decorate their homes with flowers, colourful lights and traditional oil lamps known as diyas.
The celebrations also bring families and friends together for prayers, elaborate feasts and the exchange of gifts, and lots of traditional Indian sweets.
Colourful patterns known as rangoli are created at entrances to homes, while markets bustle with shoppers buying festive essentials beneath brightly lit decorations.
Stocking up on marigolds ahead of Diwali
Potters make and paint clay lamps, or diyas, that are lit during the festival
The celebrations began on 6 November with Dhanteras, when buying gold, silver or new utensils is considered auspicious and believed to bring good fortune.
The second day, known as Chhoti Diwali, or small Diwali, is marked by the lighting of oil lamps and, in some households, setting off firecrackers.
The third day is the main celebration, when families offer evening prayers to Lakshmi, the Hindu goddess of wealth and prosperity, before gathering for festive meals and fireworks.
Offered during prayers and shared among family and friends, sweets are an integral part of the celebrations
The fourth day is celebrated differently across India, with family gatherings and New Year festivities in some communities. The fifth and final day, known as Bhai Dooj, celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters.
The festival is also celebrated by Sikhs and Jains along with other important religious observances.
Sikhs mark Bandi Chhor Divas, or Prisoner Release Day, commemorating the release of their sixth guru, Guru Hargobind, from imprisonment at Gwalior Fort in the early 17th Century.
A woman shops for lanterns in Mumbai
For Jains, Diwali marks the attainment of moksha, or liberation from the cycle of rebirth, by Lord Mahavira, the 24th and last Tirthankara, or spiritual teacher, of the current era.
With Indian communities spread across the world, Diwali is also celebrated internationally, with families and friends coming together for festive gatherings and exchanging gifts.
Parts of north India are covered with lights of every colour and shade
The festival is considered an auspicious time to make new purchases, which many believe bring prosperity and good fortune. India's stock exchanges even hold a special one-hour trading session for investors who consider buying and selling shares on Diwali favourable. Known as Muhurat trading, it will take place on 8 November this year.
Although rooted in Hindu traditions, Diwali is celebrated by people across different faiths and communities.
Pets and strays are honoured in Nepal during Diwali, where the festival is known as Tihar

title: Iran executes three men for 'armed unrest' after January protests
summary: It is claimed Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were part of anti-government protests earlier this year.
body:
Reza Zanganeh was one of the three men executed in Iran
Iran has executed three men accused of carrying out armed unrest during January's anti-government protests, according to state media.
Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were accused of throwing Molotov cocktails and grenades, using bladed weapons and firearms, and setting fire to public facilities in the city of Karaj, west of Tehran,Iran's state news agency Tasnim,externalreported.
The executions are the latest in a series linked to the protests, including those of people accused of having ties to Israel and the United States.
Thenumber of executions in Iran has increasedsince US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic began in late February.
The protest movement initially sparked in December last year by the high cost of living rapidlyevolved into widespread anti-government demonstrationsthat peaked on 8 and 9 of January.
Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths, and blamed the violence on "terrorist acts" orchestrated by the US and Israel.
However foreign-based NGOs gave higher figures andthe BBC received multiple accounts from Iraniansof security forces opening fire on unarmed protesters.
Tasnim reported that the three men were executed after the Supreme Court upheld their convictions and found them guilty of "participating in operational activities on behalf of the Israeli Zionist regime, the United States and hostile groups".
The damage allegedly included an electricity substation in Karaj which caused power outages in some areas.
Dioband was arrested on 11 January after investigations identified him as a suspect in attacks on public property and incitement to violence.
Ten others accused of taking part in the unrest under his supervision were later arrested.
Reuters news agency reports that they received prison terms of 5 to 10 years.
The latest executions in Iran come after the UN human rights chief Volker Türksaid he was alarmed by the rise in death penalties.
In August, Türk said at least 56 people had been executed on national security-related charges since 19 March, including 27 in cases linked to January's nationwide anti-government protests.
Iran is thought to be the world's second-most prolific executioner after China. Last year, it put to death at least 2,159 people, according to Amnesty International.
The human rights group said that was the highest figure on record since 1981 and included 45 executions of suspected dissidents on national security-related charges.

title: Aramco Tower hit in heart of Saudi capital as Houthis launch fresh strikes
summary: Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows damage to the building in the capital's central financial district.
body:
The Aramco Tower, a skyscraper in the Saudi Arabian capital's central financial district, had been hit by an air attack.
A statement issued via the Houthi-controlled Saba news agency confirmed the group had targeted Riyadh's business zone on Saturday, without mentioning the Aramco Tower by name.
The Saudi energy ministry said the tower had suffered only "minor damage" and no one had been killed or injured.
Footage authenticated by BBC Verify shows more extensive damage to the building, with at least one floor appearing to have been badly hit by a missile or drone strike.
Windows on more than one level appear to have been shattered by the strike.
The Houthis also said Riyadh's airport and Aramco oil storage facilities were targeted in separate strikes. Saudi Arabia said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed several missiles.
The strikes were the latest claimed by the Yemen-based armed group against targets deep inside Saudi Arabia, which the Gulf power has struggled to contain in recent months.
It came a day after the Houthisaccused a Saudi-led coalition of killing at least 33 people, including women and children, in an air strike on Yemen.
Footage broadcast by Houthi-run television channel Al Masirah showed rescuers pulling bodies from the rubble of several buildings in al-Shariyah, a town to the east of the capital, Sanaa.
Saba said 39 people had been injured in the strike. Saudi Arabia has not commented.
A Saudi-led coalition has been fighting the Houthis for more than a decade in support of Yemen's internationally recognised government, which has lost control of a large swathe of the country to the rebel group.
Although the conflict had largely been dormant in recent years, fighting has intensified following the outbreak of the Iran war.
An informal ceasefire unravelled in July after the Tehran-backed Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they have called a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport Saudi Arabia said had been to prevent an Iranian aircraft from landing there.
Major fighting has since resumed between Houthi forces and troops aligned with Yemen's Saudi-backed government.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed.

title: Nvidia launches investigation into CEO's affair with suspected Chinese spy
summary: Jensen Huang also admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and says he will cooperate with a security investigation.
body:
Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair and said he would cooperate into a security investigation launched by the tech giant
US tech giant Nvidia has opened an independent investigation following reports its CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy.
The company, one of the most valuable in the world, said its board had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, adding that the CEO was committed to continuing to lead the company.
Separately, Jensen Huang admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.
US intelligence officials believed that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for Beijing,according to a New York Times report.
Jensen Huang said he took "full responsibility" for what he did, adding that he had fallen short of his responsibilities to Nvidia's employees, board and shareholders.
Nvidia is one of the world's largest companies and seen as central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies, and Jensen Huang has been in charge of it for more than 30 years.
He said: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."
His statement continued: "Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully.
"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American."
A separate statement issued by Nvidia's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
It continued: "The Board prioritises US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders.
"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information."
US President Donald Trump said he had not spoken to the Nvidia boss since news of the investigation emerged.
"I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what's going on," Trump told reporters, adding that he had "done an amazing job for our country".
The New York Times reported in late October that Trump had been briefed last year on intelligence alleging Alice Huang was spying on China's behalf.
Asked by reporters on Sunday whether he now wished he had "acted on the intelligence" at the time, Trump responded: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honourable guy."
China has previously rejected allegations of an espionage operation targeting the Nvidia chief, describingthe claims as "groundless speculation".
Watch: Jensen Huang is a 'fine person' who has done 'an incredible job', says Trump
Jensen Huang rescued Nvidia from almost going broke on more than one occasion, and he took a punt on AI a long time before the rest of the world did.
His decision to make Nvidia chips, originally designed for gaming, become the best in the business for AI development, has now paid off in spades and the company is worth trillions.
This is a big blow for a man who is renowned for being a workaholic, a perfectionist and someone who expects incredibly high standards from his staff.
Alice Huang, who is of no relation to Jensen Huang, is linked to Singapore-based data centre firm Megaspeed.
The company told the New York Times last month its current leadership took the allegations seriously and had appointed external legal advisers to conduct an internal investigation.
Nvidia is a central player in AI infrastructure, providing chips to leading AI model developers including OpenAI and Meta.
The microchip manufacturer is worth some $4.5 trillion, making it one of the most valuable companies ever.
US intelligence agencies had been monitoring Alice Huang and concluded that she was acting on behalf of the Chinese government, according to unnamed sources cited by the New York Times.
Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking".
It remains unclear what information Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly passed to Beijing, how valuable it was, or when she is believed to have begun gathering intelligence.
Alice Huang did not respond to the paper's request for comment.
Last week, members of Congress wrote to Jensen Huang, asking him to appear before them in the light of the reported relationship.
Three House Republican committee leaders asked the CEO to appear later in the month, to talk about Nvidia's "security protocols against foreign adversary espionage" given his reported relationship with Alice Huang.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's [China's] access to sensitive US technology and information.
"The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge US technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress," the letter said.
Nvidia's AI chips have been a major focus of the rivalry between the US and China, and Washington has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold.
The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US.
In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.

title: Doing these things now will help you save money at Christmas
summary: Small decisions made now can make a big difference to your festive finances, charities say, so here are some tips.
body:
How soon is too soon when it comes to thinking about Christmas and your finances?
The answer, of course, is that it is never too soon. Save early and the cost becomes more manageable.
The squeeze is harder for some than others, with charity Barnardo's warning that some parents will skip meals so their kids get a Christmas dinner with the trimmings.
But, debt advice charity StepChange is offering tips to everyone, to avoid Christmas spending leading to a financially painful new year.
The best way to avoid a difficult January, it says, is to make a realistic plan before the spending begins.
Small decisions now can make a big difference later. Its tips include:
Budget for Christmas in full. So, that's not just presents, a budget should include the cost of food and drink, travel, parties, presents, postage, decorations and other festive extras
Spread the cost. Don't just rely on your December paypacket. Also, make a shopping list before Black Friday on 27 November - it is only a discount if you were going to buy it anyway
Book your train journey now. Advance tickets, if available, are cheaper
Set spending limits. Put a cap on the bill for Christmas socialising, and have a quiet conversation with family and friends about how much to spend on presents
Stocktake before the big food shop. Check your cupboards, fridge and freezer before you go shopping and plan meals around food you already have. Make a list of what you need and compare prices.
Think twice. Can you afford what you are going to buy? Can you afford the repayments if it's bought on credit? And, do you really need it?
"Christmas is a time when we want to enjoy ourselves and make things special for the people we care most about," said Vikki Brownridge, chief executive of StepChange.
"But it can also put a lot of pressure on household budgets, and it is key to take steps to get ahead of any January financial blues."
If you are concerned about Christmas leaving you in debt, then it is best to seek advice well before things become unmanageable.
The independent MoneyHelper website hasa guide to finding free debt advice near you,external.
There are also tools to work out if you are receiving all the benefits and grants you are entitled to, and tips on how to draw up a budget.
And it is really important to watch out for scams at this time of year. Fraudsters will take any opportunity to catch you out, especially when you are under pressure financially.

title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay
summary: The culture secretary confirms reports they could be in the list of platforms set to be banned next March.
body:
Vinted and eBay could be included in the list of platforms set to be banned for children aged under 16, the culture secretary has said.
Lisa Nandy said the government was "looking seriously" at including the retailing websites in the social media ban "to keep children safe".
The UK's social media ban for under-16s is set to come into force in March next year, with children barred from accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
In response, eBay said it was looking forward to "understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government". Vinted said it welcomed "open dialogue" with ministers and the regulator on the issue.
Asked on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme whether the government was looking to ban under-16s from Vinted and eBay, Nandy said: "We are looking seriously at doing so in order to keep children safe."
It came after theSunday Times reported,externalthat the UK's social media ban was being expanded to include the popular second-hand online marketplaces.
The move was due to fears that messaging functions on the platforms allowed strangers to groom children, according to the newspaper. It suggested similar reselling platforms, Depop and Facebook Marketplace, would also be included in the list of banned sites.
Businesses and individuals sell a host of goods on eBay, which has been a major global player in the online reselling market for years. The platform states on its website that it currently requires all of its members to be over 18 years old because listings involve "entering into a contract".
Vinted is aimed at over 18s, but its terms and conditions do allow parents or guardians to create accounts for their children, which must be used under parental supervision.
The site, on which users mostly buy and sell unwanted clothes and other fashion items, has grown rapidly recently to reach 17 million UK users.
A Vinted spokesperson said direct messaging was "part of how the platform works" but that it had a "zero tolerance for harmful or explicit content" and had moderation teams and tools to spot and remove "activity that breaks our rules".
"When we identify inappropriate behaviour, we take action, up to a permanent ban or reporting to the relevant authorities," they said.
An eBay spokesperson said the company was "focused on providing a trusted and safe marketplace experience for our millions of customers".
"While the details of the proposed legislation are not yet clear, we look forward to understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government," they added.
The government announced it would ban under-16s accessing social media in June this year, with children prevented from accessing 10 of the biggest platforms.
YouTube will also be banned for under-16s, but YouTube Kids - a version of the video-sharing app designed to be safe for children - will not be included in the measures.
A complete list of affected platforms has not yet been released, but the government said it would cover those "whose purpose is to enable social interaction and which allow users to post material".
That means platforms that have livestreaming or features that enable the potential for strangers to contact children will also be restricted, which includes gaming sites.
It does not mean that Roblox, the biggest gaming site in the UK for those aged eight to 12, for example, will be banned for under-16s. However, certain features such as its chat function will be restricted.
But Matthew Sinclair, a senior director at the Computer and Communications Industry Association, which represents tech companies, argued that ministers should prevent the rules having "scope creep".
He said a restriction on messaging for under-16s "would not stop at social media and would reach into the services families depend on to stay in touch", and urged the government to "ensure any new restrictions are proportionate and effective."
The UK's ban comes after a similar one was introduced in Australia last year.
Many children there have found ways to get round it, but the UK has said it intends to take a tougher approach.
In recent weeks, attention has turned to how a social media ban would be enforced.
Last month, the communications regulator Ofcom set out its recommendations for the most effective ways toidentify which of the UK's millions of social media users are aged over 16.
Rani Govender, head of online child safety at the NSPCC, said the "real question" going forward was how the government ensured age checks were effective.
"But effective age checks are only part of the solution," she added. "Tech companies must also be required to build child safety into every platform, device and AI tool, so children are protected from harmful and illegal content and only able to access age-appropriate services."

title: 'My mortgage is going up £200 a month': How rising interest rates are hitting people's pockets
summary: With UK interest rates set to rise, mortgages, credit cards and loans could get more expensive for millions.
body:
The BBC spoke to three people about how they could be affected by rising interest rates
On Thursday, the Bank of Englandincreased interest ratesfor the first time in over three years as it tries to get a grip on rising inflation linked to the Iran war.
Experts say there could be more hikes over the next 18 months, as the conflict continues to push up food, fuel and energy prices across the UK and worldwide.
Higher interest rates affect borrowing costs, however, which means mortgages, credit cards and personal loans could get more expensive for millions, even as savings rates improve.
For some, it could mean extra financial pressure at a time when they are already struggling with the cost of living. The BBC spoke to three people about how they could be affected.
Peter Gill says his family's costs are rising
Peter Gill, 48, is one of the around 1.3 million Britons on a variable rate mortgage.
These loans track the Bank of England base rate, with a margin on top determined by the lender, so any rise in interest rates can push up repayments.
Peter, who runs a small tiling business in Halifax, says his monthly repayments will go up by roughly £45 following Thursday's quarter-percentage point increase and he's worried they could climb higher.
But he still thinks it'd be more expensive to move onto a fixed-rate deal - which is when you pay a set amount of monthly interest for a period - and is prepared to stay put for now.
Watch: What does the raise in interest rates mean?
His higher mortgage costs come as the "cost of everything is going up", he says.
The father of two, who has a combined household income of £45,000 with his wife Faye, is having to pay his staff more because of increases in the national minimum wage. Raw material costs have also risen due to the war in Iran.
At home, the family's food, gas and electricity bills have gone up and he says he's working "about six and a half days a week" to shield them from the worst of it.
"From my point of view, inflation goes up which costs you, then interest rates go up and you have even less money."
Dawn Fazackerley-King is struggling but says there's "no more fat to trim"
Most UK mortgage holders are on fixed-rate deals, but that doesn't necessarily protect them when the Bank of England puts up rates.
David Hollingworth, from brokers L&C Mortgages, says many people will be shocked at how much higher fixed-rate deals are than they were five years agofollowing recent increases.
"Fixed rates have already risen due to market anticipation that interest rates would need to rise to combat higher inflation," he says.
Dawn Fazackerley-King is a Pilates instructor who lives near Ipswich andhas previously spoken to the BBCabout her struggles with the cost of living.
She was on a five-year fixed deal at 1.4%, which she took out in January 2022. But the mother of two is about to refix for two years and the best deal she can find is a 5.69% loan. That will push her costs up by about £200 a month.
"I don't know where that money is going to come from, it's something we are going to have to figure out as a family. It's stressful."
She and her husband, who have a joint income of about £70,000, have already gone through their direct debits and there's "no more obvious fat to trim".
There is also no scope for them to take on additional work, as they both work full time.
"We're still living in the same property, our household costs are remaining the same," Dawn says. "It's an additional cost of several hundred pounds but we're not getting anything extra for that."
Higher interest rates are "another cost to deal with", says Ben
When the Bank of England increases its base rate, credit card borrowing costs also tend to increase, although the impact is not always immediate.
It may affect people with outstanding debts, as providers can increase the interest rates they charge with 30 days' notice.
Ben Thomas, 41, from Shropshire, ditched his career as a chartered accountant during the Covid pandemic after a mental health crisis and retrained as a paramedic.
But the drop in income left him reliant on credit cards and personal loans for everyday living expenses and he is now £52,000 in debt.
Faisal Islam: How high will interest rates go?
Three ways the interest rate rise could affect you
Ben says he's reached an agreement to pause the interest on most of it, but he is still incurring charges on around £2,000 of credit card debt and is worried about his repayments going up.
"With all that's going on, rising interest rates is another cost to deal with," he tells the BBC.
As well as overall debt repayments of around £300 a month, he and his wife pay £760 on their mortgage. They have also struggled with higher food and energy bills.
Simon Trevethick is head of communications at StepChange, which has been helping Ben manage his debt. He says the debt charity has seen a 20% increase in people asking for support this year and warned of tougher times ahead.
"If higher borrowing costs feed through into household budgets over the coming months, we could see further pressure on people seeking support."

title: He spent $50,000 on Labubus but now the craze is dying
summary: Parent company Pop Mart's revenue has fallen as appetite for the quirky collectible monsters wanes.
body:
Ensito, with his custom-made Labubu teeth, posing with a new doll in his collection
For years, Labubu dolls seemed unstoppable.
Collectors young and old energetically snapped up "blind boxes" - sealed, mystery packages containing the quirky monsters - often paying $15 (£11) or more.
Those unable to get the characters they wanted were often prepared to pay much more on the resale market.
The hype around the creatures convinced a mega-fan from North Carolina, who goes by the name Ensito, to leave his tech job in 2024 to create Labubu content full-time, travelling as far as Italy and Spain to seek out the latest releases.
Ensito has spent more than $50,000 (£37,000) to build his collection of more than 400 Labubus, a figure he tells the BBC he's "embarrassed to say".
He even had a row of custom Labubu-like jagged teeth made by a dentist to wear at events.
But in recent months, Ensito's once-viral posts about the furry monsters have struggled. "Those videos used to be able to hit 10,000 really quickly but I'm struggling to do that now."
Ensito's focus has shifted to other trends like Hello Kitty and squishies.
It's a sign that the craze whichmade parent company Pop Mart worth more than US toy giants Hasbro and Mattel put togethermay be running out of steam. Analysts believe the Beijing-based brand is struggling to capture excitement beyond a single viral moment.
Pop Mart recently reported that global sales in the three months to the end of September had fallen by as much as 50% on the previous year.
The drop was particularly steep outside mainland China, with US revenue down by at least 70%.
Pop Mart didn't invent blind boxes but its dolls certainly helped to popularise them around the world.
The sales tactic made collecting feel "nostalgic", evoking the feeling of opening gifts as a child, says marketing professional Katelynn Carlson, who discovered Labubus through social media and now owns 36 of them.
One of her first Labubus was a rare doll, making the experience "even more exciting", she adds.
Labubu, which launched in 2019, has beenPop Mart's most successful line of toys. The monsters becamefashion statementsand were sported by celebrities including Kim Kardashian and Blackpink's Lisa.
They regularly attracted long queues and became so popular that Pop Mart had totemporarily pull the toys from its UK shopsafter reports of customers fighting over them. One fan paid more than$150,000 for a human-sized Labubu.
A key part of the allure was howdifficult some Labubu dolls were to find, with fans repeatedly buying blind boxes to get the version they wanted, says National University of Singapore marketing lecturer Samer El Hajjar.
Katelynn Carlson believes blind boxes were an exciting feature of the Labubu craze
Pop Mart now has 500 shops in more than 30 countries and 2,000 vending machines worldwide. The firm, which listed in Hong Kong in 2020, is worth nearly $24bn and remains one of the world's most valuable toymakers, despite its shares having fallen by more than 50% from last year's peak.
Investors worry its global success was just a viral moment rather than sustainable growth driven by long-term customer loyalty, El Hajjar says.
For Ensito, it is clear the dolls' exclusivity helped fuel the craze.
"Now it doesn't feel that way. I walk into a Pop Mart and there's a whole series of Labubus sitting there," he says.
Ashley Dudarenok of China research firm ChoZan says that sense of exclusivity faded as Pop Mart ramped up production to meet demand.
Pop Mart declined to comment on share price moves and did not respond to questions about falling sales.
As the Labubu mania cools, some of its rivals have become more popular.
Blind box collectables like Sonny Angels - tiny, unclothed cherub-like dolls - and miniature glow-in-the-dark Smiski figurines have been flying off shelves. And you can now find My Little Pony and KPop Demon Hunters in blind boxes too.
Miniso, founded in the southern Chinese city of Guangzhou, sells a range of blind-boxed Disney and Marvel characters in more than 8,000 shops globally.
"Consumers aren't particularly concerned about where the brand comes from," Miniso executive Vincent Huangsaid earlier this year. "They're more focused on the shopping experience - the designs, value for money, and enjoyment."
Pop Mart faces competition from retailers like Miniso
Experts say one of Pop Mart's biggest challenges is creating enduring characters.
That's an area where Hello Kitty brand Sanrio, which posted record earnings in the year to March, has a clear advantage, analyst Boustani suggests.
Pop Mart has invested heavily in ways to grow its brand, including setting up a theme park in Beijing andannouncing a Labubu film- following in the footsteps of franchising giants like Disney or Lego, some experts believe.
But unlike Disney, which sells a story before it sells a toy, Pop Mart is working in reverse, says Dudarenok. "The real test for next year is whether Pop Mart can make people love a character without a celebrity holding it."
Glow-in-the-dark Smiskis are emerging as a competitor to Labubus
After spending huge sums on the monsters, collector Ensito says he is now questioning how much time and money people invest in collections each time a new trend comes along. "There's always going to be a trend every year. There's always gonna be something that's gonna be really popular."
Melbourne-based content creator Lawrence Yu says that after two years of chasing Labubus, he's likely to be "more selective" before adding to his roughly 50 dolls.
His Labubu shopping and unboxing clips once drew up to a million views but the frenzy has faded and Yu rarely makes videos about them now. "I definitely think the trend has slowed down... People go crazy and then it fizzles."
Clara Barbero from Canada believes Labubus are a "dead trend" but is still keeping an eye out for interesting releases.
"I’m curating my collection more and only buying what I see myself liking for the next few years, and not just buying the newest series that’s out."
Lawrence Yu says he has spent about $1,400 on Labubu dolls
But the fluffy monsters still have truly devoted fans.
Hedy Khaled from Liverpool says although the hype around the dolls is cooling, she is just as attached to her collection of 70 Pop Mart figurines.
There's a distinction between those who chase trends and "real fans", she argues, so falling sales do not necessarily mean Labubus have lost their appeal.
For Carlson says it is the happiness the dolls bring, not the viral trend, that keeps her collecting. She still gets excited about new Pop Mart releases, like its recent cat-themed Labubu series, which has become one of her favourites.
"I think there's something special about embracing our inner child and enjoying things simply because they make us happy."

title: Nandy rejects claims of politicising Remembrance Sunday after Erasmus row
summary: The culture secretary says the UK rejoining the EU's study and work scheme will help honour wartime sacrifice.
body:
The culture secretary was interviewed by Laura Kuenssberg on Sunday
Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has rejected accusations of politicising Remembrance Sunday after being criticised for linking the event to the UK rejoining the European Union's Erasmus scheme.
Her department announced on Saturday night that "as we mark Remembrance Sunday, Erasmus+ will give a new generation the chance to build connections across Europe".
That sparked a backlash from the Conservatives, who said "veterans did not fight for a student exchange scheme" and accused her of making an "EU membership pitch".
Nandy said she was "horrified" by the Tory response and insisted that the expanded EU scheme for study and work would help young Britons recognise wartime sacrifice.
The UK isrejoining the scheme in January, six years after leaving it as part of the Brexit deal.
On Saturday, the Department for Culture, Media and Sport drew comparisons between that scheme and events on Sunday to commemorate veterans who had died in conflict.
Referring to the scheme, Nandy said in her department's press release: "As we remember the immense courage of those who served our country, we honour them by building the best opportunities for the next generation through closeness and collaboration with our allies."
Conservative Party chairman Kevin Hollinrake described her comments as "tone deaf and frankly shameful" and called on Nandy to apologise.
He said the bonds that veterans forged "run far deeper" than Erasmus.
"It is not a day for a Labour minister to try to make an EU membership pitch," he added.
Reform leader Nigel Farage told the BBC: "For Lisa Nandy to use Remembrance Sunday to announce this and say it's all about peace, it's all about the war - I find that very, very poor taste."
Peter Sharples, chief executive of the Veterans Institute, told the Telegraph that people should "just honour the fallen" on Remembrance Sunday rather than discussing "party political matters".
Asked about the criticism on the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg programme, Nandy stood by her initial remarks.
"It was Winston Churchill after the Second World War who talked about extending the hand of friendship across Europe and making sure that we honoured the legacy of that generation," she said.
She said that after Brexit "we closed off opportunities for young people from this country to understand not just the impact that generation made here in the UK, but the way in which they went off and fought for the freedom of people across Europe".
Asked to respond to accusations she had chosen Remembrance Sunday to "promote part of the new deal the government has done with the EU", Nandy said she was "not choosing today or any day actually to promote a deal with the EU".
Pressed about linking the day to what the government believes are the cultural benefits of the scheme, Nandy said: "There was a time where that wouldn't have even raised an eyebrow as somehow political, it was just common sense - and it is common sense."
The UK is paying £570m to join theexpanded Erasmus+ scheme,external, which the government said was a 30% discount. It will include free year-abroad placements for UK university students and their European peers as well as cultural exchanges.
The government said free train passes would be available for 18-year-olds to visit EU countries by themselves or with up to five friends.
Youth groups will also get to do short exchanges in other countries, with a focus on areas of the country less engaged by Erasmus previously such as the north of England and Midlands, the government said.
Applications will open for Erasmus+ later this month.
Farage described Erasmus as a "terrible scheme" and "wildly expensive" compared to theTuring Scheme,which ministers introduced in 2021 as a post-Brexit alternative.
He also criticised ongoing negotiations between the UK and the EU for a new youth mobility scheme ahead of a major summit on 20 November.
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he wants an "honest discussion"about the prospect of returning to free movement between the UK and EU.
But the EU's former Brexit negotiator Michel Barnier has warned thatthe UK cannot "cherry pick"which elements of the single market to which it subscribes.
Nandy said on Sunday that most of the benefits of Brexit promised in 2016 "have not been realised" and "there are trade-offs and choices to be made" on Britain's future relationship with the EU.

title: Parliament restoration delays 'frustrating', says Commons Speaker
summary: Sir Lindsay Hoyle urges action after a committee warns it is "crunch time" for the ailing building.
body:
The Speaker of the House of Commons has expressed "frustration" with the lack of progress on restoration to protect the Palace of Westminster.
Sir Lindsay Hoyle told the BBC the current process for approving essential renovations to Parliament amounted to "putting ourselves in handcuffs", and said more time was spent "doing surveys" than getting repairs under way.
The Commons public accounts committee this week warned it was "crunch time" for the ailing building's restoration, which could cost up to £40bn and take 61 years.
It said every additional year of delay cost taxpayers £420m, while its chairman warned the Palacecould be left vulnerable to a devastating firelike that which engulfed the Notre Dame.
Sir Lindsay said his "biggest frustration" with the Victorian building's restoration was that "we're not getting on with the work".
"We spend more time doing surveys," he toldBBC Radio 4's The Week in Westminster. "Instead of doing surveys, why don't we start repairing the building?"
The Speaker criticised current legislation which means the main renovations cannot begin until Parliament has approved the entire project's scope and funding.
"It's very frustrating when the Act of Parliament prevents you carrying out the major repairs that you need to. Talk about putting ourselves in handcuffs."
He added: "What we have to do is renovate and repair the problems areas."
More asbestos found in Parliament, as MPs urged to get on with revamp
Parliament revamp could cost £40bn and take 61 years
Sir Lindsay also questioned why a fire-suppressing mist system had not yet been introduced throughout the building, even though he has called for it for years.
"The major part and the most historic parts of the building haven't got it, and that's what we need."
Asked about reports that Parliament might be given an opportunity to vote on the way forward before the end of 2026, Sir Lindsay said that was a matter for government business managers.
"Who knows when it's going to come forward? Let's see what the House decides," he said.
Much of the 19th-Century building's network of wires and pipes dates back to the 1940s - and some to the Victorian era - according to areport,externalwhich warned of an "impending crisis" a decade ago. Fire safety issues and high levels of asbestos have also been identified.
The BBC understands government whips have discussed holding a debate and vote by the new year, but no date has been scheduled.
This would decide whether to proceed with up to £3bn of initial works and narrow down four current options, ahead of a final decision by 2030.
One proposed option would see MPs and peers move out of the site for up to 24 years from 2032, costing up to £15.6bn.
Another involves moving only the House of Lords out of the building, costing £39bn and taking 61 years.
The chairman of the body in charge of refurbishing Parliamentdefended the potential costs earlier this year, telling the BBC: "We're already spending £150m a year trying to keep the thing standing."

title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law
summary: The government argues the change will help jobseekers and could help to prevent pay discrimination.
body:
Andy Burnham says it isn't fair if an employer 'holds all the cards'
Businesses should publish salaries in job adverts now, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is telling firms, rather than wait for a new law to come in that will force them to do so.
The government is planning to make pay details compulsory in adverts, with legislation on the issue being brought forward "as soon as possible".
It argues the change will help jobseekers, particularly those applying for their first job, and could help prevent pay discrimination. However, one industry group said setting pay was a complex process and regulating adverts was not always suitable.
It comes a week after the UK's equality watchdog saidemployees should legally be able to find out what their colleagues are earning.
Burnham said the current system felt "weighted against the applicant" and the changes were aimed at "tilting the scales back".
"It can be quite soul destroying for young people these days, applying for jobs when the salary is not listed but sometimes they're not getting a reply," he told the BBC.
The prime minister added that publishing salaries in adverts was also important for closing the gender pay gap.
He was also challenged over whether MPs should be disclosing salaries when advertising for staff in their offices.
A number of politiciansare currently advertising for roles without giving an expected salary.,external
Burnham said: "It would apply completely to them too and the call I'm making today is, before the law changes do it voluntarily because it's the right thing to do."
The Cabinet Office launched a consultation into pay and reducing discrimination in the summer, and the government said there had been "overwhelming support" for greater transparency, with 94% of respondents backing the move.
"Whether you're a young person starting out or a parent trying to support your family, you should know what a job pays before spending your time and effort applying for it," Burnham said.
The government said the move was part of attempts to reduce the nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" - ahead of the final report of the Milburn Review into youth inactivity, which is due in the coming weeks.
Publishing salary details upfront could "expose unjustified differences in pay, give workers greater confidence to challenge discrimination and prevent disagreements over pay escalating into disputes".
The proposals are similar tomeasures being introduced in the European Union.,external
Employers in Europe will have to disclose the initial pay or range for new roles, which must either be included in a published job advert or shared before an interview.
According to data from UK jobs website Adzuna,external, 51% of the adverts on its site in September had salary information, but the proportion has been falling in recent years.
Adzuna co-founder Andrew Hunter said being open about pay "should be the norm, not the exception".
He added that employers who put a salary on a job advert "attract more applicants, and better-suited ones".
Previous research from the CIPD,external, an industry body for human resources managers, has indicated that the public sector and charities are more likely to reveal pay information that private firms, while pay ranges were more common than specific salaries.
But it found not all employers were "fully transparent", with pay ranges sometimes wider than £10,000.
CIPD chief executive Neil Carberry said that while, in principle, giving salary details was "a good thing", in practice it was "more complicated".
"There isn't always a single fixed figure, and employers will want to set pay based on a candidate's skills, experience and potential."
Carberry added the process was complex, saying that drafting job adverts is "best left to good employer practice rather than government regulation".
The government has said it will set out further details on what information will be required and how the legislation will be enforced "in due course".
Conservative shadow business secretary Julia Lopez said: "At a time when employers are finding it harder and harder to take on staff, Labour have decided to make their lives even more difficult.
"It should be up to businesses to decide what information they advertise about job openings, and to decide how to attract the best applicants.
"As long as they are not being dishonest, misleading or discriminatory, it should not be a matter for the government."
Last week, the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC), said publishing salaries in job adverts would be a "positive step".
It also said bosses should be required to respond to questionnaires about colleagues' pay to cut pay discrimination.
At present, employers do not have to respond to employee requests for salary information about their co-workers.
The EHRC also said employers should be prevented from asking about current salary when offering a job to stop a history of discrimination from continuing.
Employers in the UK are currently allowed to ask you how much you get paid in your current role, butapplicants are under no obligation to tell them.

title: Burnham responds to BBC question over Labour's past links to Brand
summary: The prime minister says that Labour politicians courting the comedian a decade ago had not been aware of his crimes.
body:
In 2014 Burnham posted a supportive message on social media when Brand was facing media criticism about his housing arrangements
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said Russell Brand has rightly been held to account for his "horrific" crimes and sought to explain Labour's previous association with the comedian.
Some within the Labour Party attempted to court Brand's support more than a decade ago, before police began investigating him - and in 2014 Burnham posted a supportive message on social media when the comedian was facing media criticism about his housing arrangements.
Asked about the 2014 tweet on Friday, Burnham said: "It's not always the case that people know everything about people in public life."
Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault on Thursday.
In 2014, Brand was writing regular opinion pieces for newspapers and appearing on political discussion programmes, including the BBC's Question Time.
His anti-establishment and left-wing views had also gained him a following on social media.
The same year, Burnham, then the shadow health secretary, posted on Twitter in support of Brand following allegations about the comedian's housing arrangements.
It is not clear what Burnham had been referring to in his 2014 tweet, but the previous day, The Sun claimed Brand had paid rent at a property owned by a landlord in a tax haven, while at the same time campaigning against tax avoidance.
Brand threatened to sue the newspaper and said he would give the money to victims of the Hillsborough disaster, a group Burnham has long campaigned for.
At the time, Burnham said it was "depressing to see media mission to discredit someone who stops playing their game" and urged Brand to "keep going".
Asked about that social media post on Friday, Burnham told the BBC "all I can say is I had no idea of the full extent of what he was doing or what he went on to do".
The PM added: "His [Brand's] crimes are horrific, he's rightly been held to account, justice for the victims and that is the right course that's been taken here.
"It's not always the case that people know everything about people in public life, but what is important is that where there is wrongdoing it is exposed."
The prime minister added: "Credit to the victims, huge credit, the courage that it's taken, but also the journalists who've exposed this."
Ed Miliband, then the Labour leader, was interviewed by Brand in the run-up to the 2015 general election.
Brand, who had previously dismissed the idea of voting, backed Labour following the interview, saying Miliband had convinced him that "this bloke will listen to us".
Miliband, who is now foreign secretary, has previouslysaid he regrets being interviewed by Brand.
On Friday, a spokesman for Miliband told the BBC: "These are horrific crimes that Russell Brand has been found guilty of and Ed's profound sympathy is with the victims.
"As he said in 2023, 'of course, knowing what I know now - and I was not aware of these allegations at the time about Russell Brand - I wouldn't have done that interview and I regret doing it'."
Brand was found not guilty of two other counts of rape, and one count of attempted indecent assault.
During a four-week trial, Brand faced allegations from six women spanning the decade between 1999 and 2009.
The 51-year-old was refused bail and will spend the weekend in custody before he is due to return to court on Monday for sentencing.

title: Policing needs reform to cope with modern criminals, Met Police chief warns
summary: The Met Police chief used a speech to argue that the current policing system in England and Wales is "heading for failure" without urgent change.
body:
Watch: 'Degradation of policing' by not reforming force, says Met chief
The police system in England and Wales cannot cope against sophisticated modern criminals without urgent reform, the head of the Metropolitan Police has said.
In a speech on Friday, Sir Mark Rowley argued the system was "heading for failure" without change.
He is proposing eight to 10 regional police forces, supported by hundreds of local policing commands and a new national force, in what would be the biggest overhaul of policing since the 1960s.
The changes would replace the 43-force structure with three tiers: local teams dealing with neighbourhood issues, regional forces sharing specialist resources and a National Police Service tackling the most serious crimes.
In January it seemed that the many senior police officers were in favour of creating a National Police Service, and that organising into much larger regional forces had won the argument.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmoodproduced a white paperthat aligned with their ideas and asked the former Metropolitan Police Commissioner Lord Hogan-Howe to look at what the force boundaries might be.
But everything changed in July when Andy Burnham became prime minister. So far, Burnham has not spoken publicly about the plans, and the police chiefs are nervous that they may not have his backing. That may be why they have come out so strongly today, warning of the potentially apocalyptic effect of doing nothing.
As well as pushing hard for large regional forces, they are also making an argument about money which is familiarfrom the defence funding argument.
Sir Mark also pointed out that police funding in England and Wales has fallen from 0.9% of GDP to 0.7%. Implicit in that is that while the slice of the cake being allocated to defending the country is growing, the slice being allocated to defending people's communities and their homes is getting smaller.
Labour wants to shake up the police - but will that solve 'everyday crime epidemic'?
Number of police forces to be cut in major shake-up
Court system under massive strain, warns Met chief
In his speech, Sir Mark saidorganised crime groups, fraud networks, cyber-criminals and those involved in online child abuse increasingly operate across regional and international borders, while police forces remain organised around local areas.
"The victim remains local but increasingly the threat does not," he said citing the example of children who are "groomed by predators on another continent".
He argued that the current system is struggling to keep pace with these threats, saying: "We have 43 overstretched forces trying to do too much, with too little."
Merging forces would reduce duplication and could free up thousands of roles to be redirected towards front line policing, he believes.
Speaking on BBC Breakfast prior to his speech, Sir Mark said crime had changed a lot over the years but the police was largely organised how it was 60 years ago.
"Obviously the world's moved on a long way in that time."
His proposals follow a consultation launched by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood in January. This included plans for a National Police Service to tackle the most complex crimes and a possible merger of the 43 forces into fewer, larger forces.
However some rural police and crime commissioners have described the plans as "political manoeuvring" by larger forces to "load the dice in their favour".
Dorset Police and Crime Commissioner David Sidwick reiterated his strong opposition to proposals to merge the forces.
"My concern is simple. If funding is diverted away from frontline services in Dorset to establish new national structures, local communities could end up receiving less rather than more."
In addition, Kent's Conservative police and crime commissioner Matthew Scott said: "[Sir Mark believes] policing should suffer a decade of disruption, that local policing services should be cut back and made more remote, and that this can all be done without ever asking the public what they want from their local police force."
The Association of Police and Crime Commissioners (APCC) has also questioned whether merging forces is the best way to improve policing.
It said: "The case for modernisation and a National Police Service is clear. The case for reducing 43 forces to nine regional 'mega-forces' is not."
Outgoing Cheshire Chief Constable Mark Roberts also said a future policing model needs to be built in a way that retains the places that already work well so that they do not "get subsumed" and end up "scrabbling to try and get resource from some of the metropolitan areas"
"Bigger isn't always better - we see some high performing big forces, we see some poorer performing big forces.
"The aim is to raise everyone at least to the minimum standard of the best," Roberts said after Rowley's speech.
Asked on Breakfast what would happen if the reforms were not put in place, Sir Mark said: "the risk is failure".
"Failure means solving fewer crimes, less local presence, when you get exceptional incidents like a certain outbreak of disorder like we saw in Hampshire."
In September police clashed withanti-migrant protesters in Portsmouthwhen 120 migrants arrived in a single dinghy.
"Standing still looks like a degradation of policing day by day, struggling even more as criminals outpace policing because we're not organised to meet it," Sir Mark added.
A Home Office spokesperson defended the plans, saying: "Our current model of policing has not changed since the 1960s and is no longer fit for purpose."
Sir Mark has also highlighted the financial pressures facing policing, saying that spending on policing had fallen from about 0.9% of GDP to 0.7% since 2010, which he said was as "a big hit".
"We do need investment as well, but if you threw loads of money at the current system it's still not going to fix the fundamental problem, it's not designed to meet today's challenges," he told the BBC.
"Throwing money at the current system isn't going to work."
Sir Mark said in his speech that years of underinvestment hasleft forces relying on ageing technology, and officers are increasingly diverted from neighbourhood policing to deal with other demands, including mental health and social care.
He also pointedto falling police performance, saying positive outcomes nationally are now less than half the level they were 12 years ago, while public confidence has fallen by 9%.
